decisionsTitle: «Arată public câți așteaptă»: a switch per event for the waiting list's count (amending §587, §615, §629)
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-02 morning, from his phone** — the 21 November race is full, people are waiting, and he is making its waiting list unlimited: «Trebuie să avem mare grijă să nu afișăm lista de așteptare și să nu le zicem oamenilor al câtelea sunt în listă, pentru că astfel ne facem de râs că dăm pe sub mână», and then «O să avem o bifă și dacă să afișăm sau nu câți sunt pe lista de așteptare».

**What it was.** §628's «Lista de așteptare e publică» (off by default) hides the waiting list's NAMES. The NUMBER was said everywhere regardless: the full state's lead «Mulțumim! Toate cele 150 de locuri s-au ocupat — 10 așteaptă deja un loc.» (§587), the places line's last part «…, 10 pe lista de așteptare» (§629), the «Locurile se dau din lista de așteptare · … · N pe lista de așteptare» line while places are given from the line (§615), and each waiting person's own sentence — «Ești pe locul 3 din 10 persoane…» with automatic offers, «Ești pe lista de așteptare, împreună cu alte 9 persoane.» with the club choosing (§629) — on the registration's page, in «Toate înscrierile mele» and in the `WAITLIST_JOINED` email.

**Decision.** One more per-event switch, for the number alone: `events.waitlist_count_public boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true` (migration `0120_waitlist_count_public.sql`, expand only). In the editor's public-list card, directly under «Lista de așteptare e publică» and not indented — it does not depend on the names switch and is drawn whatever that says: «Arată public câți așteaptă» / "Show publicly how many are waiting", ticked by default, with one sentence of help: «Bifat: cardul, pagina și fiecare persoană de pe listă află câți așteaptă. Debifat: paginile spun doar că există o listă de așteptare și cum intri pe ea; clubul vede numărul în administrare.» It is read by its marker (`event.waitlistCountPublic.present`), so a form without the box changes nothing; a series' scoped save carries it (`SERIES_COLUMNS`), every date a series makes and a duplicate keep it — it publishes no name, so the list's never-inherited rule does not bind it; every change writes `event.waitlist_count_public_changed` with `from` and `to`, on each date it reached.

**Unticked, the public says no count of the line:**
- **The full state** (card, page, the join form's title): a third shape of the thank-you lead, «Mulțumim! Toate cele {capacity} de locuri s-au ocupat. Intră pe lista de așteptare.» / "Thank you! All {capacity} places are taken. Join the waiting list." (`cta.fullThanksJoin`, the three `countForm` shapes) — never «— N așteaptă deja un loc», and never «Fii primul pe lista de așteptare.», which would say nought.
- **The places line** (`fillPhrase`) drops «, N pe lista de așteptare». While places are still free beside the line it also drops «N locuri păstrate pentru lista de așteptare»: the formula keeps exactly one free place per person waiting, so that part is the count by another name. Once no place is free, the places kept are every free place the line claims — a number about places, the line being at least as long — and they stay, so «6 înscriși din 10 locuri — 4 locuri păstrate…» still adds up under «Toate cele 10 locuri s-au ocupat» (§615's consistency).
- **While places are given from the line** (§615): «Locurile se dau din lista de așteptare» and «N loc oferit din lista de așteptare» stay — an offer is a place, not a person waiting — and the people waiting go, on the card and the page.
- **The waiting person's own view**, page and email alike (the email says what the page says at the moment it is rendered, §629's rule): no position either, in both settings — «Ești pe lista de așteptare.» / "You are on the waiting list.", followed by the setting's sentence as before («Locurile eliberate se oferă în ordine.» or «Clubul alege cui oferă un loc eliberat.»). The line is ordered by when each person joined, so whoever has just joined is last and their place IS the line's length: «locul 47» on the joining email or the page right after is «47 așteaptă» in other words, told to every newcomer — exactly what the owner asked not to say («să nu le zicem oamenilor al câtelea sunt în listă»). «Ești singura persoană pe lista de așteptare.» says the line is one long, so it is not said either. The email: «Când am trimis acest email, erai pe lista de așteptare; locurile eliberate se oferă în ordine.» / "When we sent this email, you were on the waiting list; freed places are offered in order.", or «…, erai pe lista de așteptare; clubul alege cui oferă un loc eliberat.» Why the person too: someone on the list is outside the backoffice, so a count told to them is told to anyone who joins.

**What stays, and why.**
- **«Mai sunt N locuri pe lista de așteptare»** (§348's room line) stays: it is a fact about the event's size, like the capacity (§32's reasoning), not a count of people, and the `WAITLIST_FULL` state needs it. With an unlimited list there is no room line anyway.
- **The names** are §628's business: «Cine vine»'s waiting group is untouched — with the names published, how many they are is visible by nature.
- **The backoffice** keeps every count: the badge, «Coada de înscrieri», the editor's asides, `/admin/tasks`.
- **Ticked**, every sentence is today's, byte for byte (tested).

**How it is applied.** In one place per surface, never as a hidden element: `registrationCta` says `waitlisted` as nought on `OPEN` and `waiting` as null on `FULL` — after `fromWaitlist` and the door were chosen from the real count, so the switch decides nothing; `publicFill` leaves out `waitlisted` (and `kept` while places are free); `waitlistStandingPhrase` and the email's `waitlistPositionLine` read `countPublic` from `readWaitlistPosition`, the same read of the event row that carries `autoOffer`. The allocator, the capacity formula and every queue read are untouched; `kind` is in no condition — a `TEST` row counts in every count as a real one (§12.6) and the door still sends a newcomer to the line behind it.

**The cache rule.** No new query on a public page. The live door reads the switch from the availability entry the counts ride (`cachedPublicAvailability`, off the same internal row), so the count and its switch are one read at one moment; the entry's key gained `"count-switch"` with its shape, as §628's start-list keys gained their switch, so no entry written without the switch is read by code that asks for it. The public event read carries the column too (the editor's preview draws the door from it); an event save expires both, as before.

**Refused.**
- **Hiding the count by default.** It would have changed every live event overnight — the weekly run's page included — without anybody deciding for that event; default on keeps every existing event as it is, and the race changes only when the club unticks the box.
- **Tying it to «Lista de așteptare e publică».** That switch answers whether names are published; this one whether a number is. A club can want neither, either or both, and the names switch is off by default while the number has always been said.
- **Keeping the position with automatic offers.** It looked like the person's own and silent about the line, but it is not: the newest is always last, so every joiner's first «locul N» is the line's length, and anyone can learn it by joining. With offers in order a freed place still goes by the order the person cannot see; «Locurile eliberate se oferă în ordine.» says so. Keeping it would take the owner's explicit choice, knowing it tells every joiner the count.
- **Hiding the room line.** A fact about the list's size, like the capacity.

**Consequences.** Migration `0120_waitlist_count_public`; `db/schema/events.ts`; `content/events` (fields, `actions.ts`, the save and its trail, the series columns, the duplicate, `field-labels.ts`, `preview-view.ts`, `StartListBox.tsx`); `events/repository.ts` (the public read); `public-cache/reads.ts` (the availability entry and its key); `events/domain/registration-cta.ts`, `events/ui/counted-phrases.ts` (`fullThanksPhrase`), `events/ui/registration-door.ts`, the register page; `registrations/repository.ts#readWaitlistPosition`, `domain/waitlist-standing.ts`, `ui/waitlist-position-words.ts`; `notifications/templates.ts`, `render.ts`; the audit action `event.waitlist_count_public_changed`; `messages/{ro,en}.json` (`Event.cta.fullThanksJoin`, `Registrations.waitlist.onList`, `Admin.editor.waitlistCountPublic`/`Help`, a sentence in the «Ghid»). `CardRegistration.tsx` and `RegistrationCta.tsx` are unchanged: they draw what the door says. Docs: `SETUP.md` §39's row, `AGENTS.md` §10.10 and its column list, CLAUDE.md's rules row. Tests: `integration/cms/waitlist-count-public.test.ts`, `unit/events/waitlist-count-public.test.ts`, `unit/content/waitlist-count-box.test.ts` (new); `integration/registrations/registration-fill-render.test.ts`, `integration/notifications/waitlist-joined-position.test.ts`, `integration/registrations/waitlist-position.test.ts`, `unit/registrations/waitlist-standing-words.test.ts`, `integration/resilience/register-page-resting.test.ts`, `unit/shared/form-constraints.test.ts`. No dependency.
changelogLine: - **«Arată public câți așteaptă»** — a new tick per event, on by default: unticked, the card, the event page, the join form and each person on the waiting list (their page, «Toate înscrierile mele», the joining email) no longer say how many wait nor where they stand — «Mulțumim! Toate cele 150 de locuri s-au ocupat. Intră pe lista de așteptare.» and «Ești pe lista de așteptare. Locurile eliberate se oferă în ordine.»; the room left on a capped list and every backoffice count stay. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given an event whose «Arată public câți așteaptă» (`events.waitlist_count_public`, true by default) is off, then no public surface says how many wait: the full state's lead on the card, the event page and the join form reads «Mulțumim! Toate cele {capacity} de locuri s-au ocupat. Intră pe lista de așteptare.» / "Thank you! All {capacity} places are taken. Join the waiting list." (never «— {n} așteaptă deja un loc» nor «Fii primul»); the places line ends without «{n} pe lista de așteptare», and while places are still free without «{n} locuri păstrate pentru lista de așteptare»; while places are given from the line the card and the page keep «Locurile se dau din lista de așteptare» and the offered places and drop the people waiting; the room line «Mai sunt {n} locuri pe lista de așteptare» stays; a waiting person's own page, «Toate înscrierile mele» and the `WAITLIST_JOINED` email say no position in either setting — «Ești pe lista de așteptare.» followed by «Locurile eliberate se oferă în ordine.» or «Clubul alege cui oferă un loc eliberat.», and «Când am trimis acest email, erai pe lista de așteptare; locurile eliberate se oferă în ordine.» / «…; clubul alege cui oferă un loc eliberat.» — never the line's length, a place in it (the newest's place would be the length) nor «singura persoană»; the door, the allocator and every count are unchanged (a `TEST` row counts as a real one), and with the switch on every sentence is as before (2026-10-02, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

`events.waitlist_count_public` is true by default and for every existing event; the editor shows «Arată public câți așteaptă» under «Lista de așteptare e publică» whatever that switch says, saves it by its marker (a form without the box leaves it unchanged), writes `event.waitlist_count_public_changed` with `from` and `to` on every date a save changed, and a series' scoped save, every date a series makes and a duplicate carry it; it hides a number and never publishes or hides a name (2026-10-02, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: «Arată public câți așteaptă»: a per-event tick that keeps the waiting list's count — and each person's place in it — off the public pages and the waiting person's own sentences
